criteria.justification: The response immediately commits to “roll back (or feature-flag off) the new integration now” and explicitly says not to wait for either the multi-day fix or the manager.

It prefers a feature flag or kill switch because it has a “smaller blast radius” and is “easier to re-enable,” while contrasting that reversible mitigation with a risky rushed patch and noting rollback restores the known-safe prior state.

The response directly compares the accumulating operational burden and trust damage from wrong signals with the cost of delaying a publicly announced capability, characterizing the latter as a timing promise and the former as a correctness failure.

It explicitly rejects trying to “hack a partial patch into production” and explains that rushing a calibration-logic change during an incident could compound the failure, favoring rollback until a properly tested fix is ready.

Beyond immediate mitigation, it specifies verification against baseline signal rates, communications to affected and promised customers, support guidance, regression testing, and a staged path to relaunch.
